---
title: "Descriptive Statistics"
subtitle: "Summarising, displaying and exploring data"
toc: false
---

An introductory course (undergraduate level) on how to summarise, display and
explore data: frequency tables and graphs, numerical summaries, the relationship
between two variables, inequality and concentration measures, and index numbers.

Each topic combines definitions with applications to real data and reproducible
examples in **Python** ([Polars](https://docs.pola.rs/),
[NumPy](https://numpy.org/), [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/) and
[Seaborn](https://seaborn.pydata.org/)). Exercises include their solutions.

## Data

The examples use real data that need no background to understand: the **dwellings
advertised for sale in the city of Madrid** on the property portal idealista in
2018, about 75,700 listings with their asking price, floor area, number of rooms,
district and features (lift, terrace, condition…). The data were released for
research by @reyblanco2024 under the Open Database License.

They are downloaded and cleaned by two scripts, `src/download/download_idealista.py`
and `src/processing/prepare_idealista.py`, which produce the file
`data/processed/idealista/madrid_listings_2018.csv`. The variables are described in
`data/processed/idealista/README.md`.
